board_feedback: 2026-10-13: user confirmed switching blackout was reduced into an acceptable range. This is not zero-blackout, optical timing, or exhaustive cold-boot/stress certification.
historical_releases: Superseded bits archived outside the project; recover from Git commit 7e0a353 or rubbish/secondary_player_release_20261013. Original release metadata retained in seed/release_history.

player.change: Removed fixed-pattern comparison, switch trace, screen-confirm/copy controls and diagnostic-only paths. Kept linkage, real emergency caching, configuration, manual playback, serial protocol and fallback behavior.
player.validation: Build/self-test, 940x750 and 1600x1000 UI renders, real H264/AAC media test and cache handoff passed; see seed/continuous_carrier/player_cache_validation.xml.

fix: Qualified PC presence selects the recovered pixel/serial carrier, independent of UART permission. Native pixels follow the actual PC raster; a common symbol pipeline and four-lane serializer preserve clock, sync and information packets across frame-boundary authorization. Unauthorized PCM becomes valid silence. FIFO errors reset capture/parsing and revoke old authorization without changing the still-valid carrier. Pixel-only clock recovery drains old SDRAM read ACKs and resumes cached publication, including toggle zero. Registered FIFO watermark and equivalent glyph selection close actual critical paths.
limits: Physical HDMI loss/format change still switches carrier and can cause monitor relock. A mid-packet revocation may invalidate that packet; subsequent complete PCM packets are valid silence. Supported source remains RGB8 SDR 720p and stereo layout-0 LPCM. Simulation cannot determine the monitor's optical blackout duration or certify real TF/network/audio behavior. User accepted reduced switching blackout; no claim of zero blackout.
simulation_limits: Common-output test uses actual renderer/TMDS encoder, full 1650x750 raster, AVI and PCM/BCH vectors with storage/network stubs. Ingress uses real vendor IOL/PLL models and UART, but stubbed media/network and a source without audio islands; GOOD_FRAMES=1 and settle=64 accelerate only the test (production 8 and 50000). A separate reproduction proves the vendor PLL's floating-point false loss at 2^26ns for 13.33ns stimulus. Final ingress uses 1fs resolution and binary-exact 13.34375ns period/about 74.941MHz, runs to 68.186ms with all 5 checks passing. Vendor model and production clocks were not modified or forced locked.
drc: No multi-drive or abnormal timing path; existing PHY7002 and PHY5079 warnings retained. Both real common-clock mux modes timed; no new broad CDC timing exclusions. Bitgen dependency/timing gate passed; all 96 input hashes matched the routed build.
expected: Use rebuilt player with the unchanged accepted secondary bit; no reflash for this UI cleanup. PC HDMI to A, display to B. Keep main bit and TF assets. Connect COM, select AnlogicHDMI75 and enable linkage; no diagnostic comparison controls remain. Normal/emergency video, cached first frame and stop-to-local behavior are retained. Physical source insertion/loss can still relock.
